about: A line stands in an own lock by its signature — a key the tree admits signed it, inside its window and its coverage of the place — withdrawal or not. `--place <place>`, as many as a batch needs, names the own locks a batch speaks to: each own line lands in every named place that admits it, so the same bytes land at seven places in one act, and a line no named place admits refuses the batch. With no place named, a line lands in the one own lock that admits it, and one two own locks admit is refused, naming --place.

cases.name: a lane-B own line with --place nosuch, on a copy of the tree at epoch 260
cases.said: REFUSE·place nothing landed · nosuch is no place of the tree

cases.name: the same line with --place topos-json, which lane-B does not cover
cases.said: REFUSE·nowhere: no place of topos-json takes it

cases.name: the same line with --place bound
cases.acts: every place · then the root · 0 lines to the ledger · 1 to bound's own lock

cases.name: its withdrawal, with no place named
cases.acts: every place · then the root · 0 lines to the ledger · 1 to bound's own lock

red was: identical lines at seven places admitted nowhere
